_README: Hand-authored ANALYSIS specs (sub-step 3c). Each entry is one analysis — a comparison/finding OVER conditions (leaderboard, hypothesis test, sweep, ...). The generator (scripts/generate_post_run_report.py) validates these, attaches provenance, and emits results/analyses-manifest.json (+ .md). HYBRID authoring: the machine-fillable keys (analysis_id, type, conditions_compared, output_path) are authored here; the human-authored fields (outcome, hypothesis_refs, preregistered, deviations, predicted_outcome, tie_set, paper_section, working_notes_obs) may stay null until a human writes the finding + preregistration linkage, per the schema's lenient back-fill. Set manually_verified_at when a human has authored/verified a row. Schema: docs/manifest-schemas/analyses-manifest.schema.json.

analyses._note: The N=1 single-pass baseline leaderboard at 384px (the cross-architecture model x modality x thinking x temperature matrix). FINDING (authored 2026-06-03; REVISED twice same day: E57 genuine-Pro replace, then the n=3 completeness top-up): tie_set + outcome from a round-robin tile-swap permutation (replicate-mean per-tile, 10k perms, seed 42, two-sided) + Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (q=0.05) + greedy-clique tiering at the 20 m headline buffer -> 7 tiers (129/153 pairs significant); Tier 1 (tie_set) = TWO genuine-Pro text cells at T=0.0 -- pro-text-high-t-0-0 (n1-pro-rerun-384, F1 0.804) + pro-text-medium-t-0-0 (pv-diag-384, F1 0.792) -- statistically indistinguishable, both clear of the Tier-2 pair (the two Pro-text T=0.7 cells, 0.755/0.745). All four anti-diagonal Pro cells are the genuine-Pro re-run (n1-pro-rerun-384), REPLACING the Flash-misdispatched n1-outstanding cells (E57), and all four medium-thinking Pro cells were brought to n=3 (the pv-diag medium-t-0-0 run_1 had ~5% unretried tile failures that had depressed its score; recovered to 487/487 -- Obs 338/339). The intermediate 'sole leader' result (pre-top-up) was an artefact of that incomplete run_1. Result artefacts: results/paper-eval/n1/384px-14buf-mcc/tiering/tiering_20m.{json,md}; script: scripts/n1_baseline_leaderboard_tiering.py. This single-pass board is the baseline comparator the consensus (H3) and proposer-verifier (H2) architectures are measured against. See docs/methodology/n1-baseline-matrix.md and planning/leaderboard-construction-plan.md.
analyses.predicted_outcome: Preregistered directions come from earlier Gemini-3-Flash / 512 px phases (this board is Gemini 3 at 384 px): H6 (Phase 4, the only untested confirmatory hypothesis) expected the stronger Pro model to transfer/match-or-exceed Flash; H7 (Phase 2b) found T=0.0 optimal for both tracks; H1 (Phase 2a) planned a text-only vs image-using contrast without a committed directional winner. Board result (genuine Pro, all Pro cells n>=3): H6 holds strongly and uniformly -- the top six cells are all genuine Pro, every Pro-text cell beats the best Flash cell (flash-image-minimal-t-0-0, F1 0.600), and the genuine Pro-image cells match Flash on F1 while dominating MCC (any apparent Flash-over-Pro in the raw board traces to the E57 Flash-misdispatched cells, now replaced). H7's T=0.0 optimum is cleanly supported within Pro text: the two Tier-1 cells are both T=0.0 (HIGH and MEDIUM thinking, tied) and the two Tier-2 cells are both T=0.7 -- a clear T=0.0 > T=0.7 ordering at matched model/modality. H1 resolves metric-dependently -- text wins F1@20 m localisation (the top four cells are all text) while image wins MCC tile-discrimination (pro-image-medium-t-0-7, MCC +0.911).
analyses.outcome: At the preregistered 20 m buffer the best single pass for mound localisation is genuine Gemini 3 Pro text at T=0.0. Tier 1 -- the tie_set -- is a two-member statistical tie between pro-text-high-t-0-0 (F1 0.804) and pro-text-medium-t-0-0 (F1 0.792): a round-robin tile-swap permutation (BH-FDR q=0.05; 129/153 pairs significant -> 7 tiers) cannot separate them, and both are significantly clear of the Tier-2 pair -- the two Pro-text T=0.7 cells, pro-text-medium-t-0-7 (0.755) and pro-text-high-t-0-7 (0.745). So at T=0.0 the thinking level (HIGH vs MEDIUM) does not significantly matter, and T=0.0 beats T=0.7 (Tier 1 vs Tier 2) at matched model and modality (H7). The top four cells are all Pro text and the top six all genuine Pro; the text-over-image advantage holds at matched settings (best Pro text 0.804 vs best Pro image 0.666). The F1 leaders are NOT the tile-level discrimination (MCC) leader: genuine Pro IMAGE wins MCC -- pro-image-medium-t-0-7 (MCC +0.911, but 9th on F1) and pro-image-high-t-0-0 (+0.868) -- while Pro text leads F1, so the best single-pass configuration is metric-dependent. (All eight Pro cells are genuine Gemini 3 Pro at n>=3; see deviations E57 and docs/methodology/n1-baseline-matrix.md for board provenance.)

analyses._note: Diversity-dividend test (H3): a combined, statistically tiered leaderboard placing 4 consensus pool-champions (best (N, threshold) operating point per proposer pool at T=0.7, the production carry-forward temperature) against the 18 single-pass cells of n1-baseline-matrix-384. Per the preregistered H3 analysis plan (analysis-summary.md: 'compare voted F1 vs single-pass mean F1' + 'threshold sweep curves showing optimal (N, threshold) combinations'), the best operating point against the known test-tile ground truth IS the characterisation deliverable -- not an in-sample limitation. Run with the project-canonical n1 method (scripts/consensus_vs_baseline_tiering.py reuses n1_baseline_leaderboard_tiering verbatim): round-robin tile-swap micro-F1 permutation (10k, seed 42, two-sided) + BH-FDR q=0.05 + greedy-clique tiering at the 20m headline buffer. Consensus cells contribute integer per-tile TP/FP/FN from their single aggregated set; single-pass cells keep the pass-averaged per-tile counts. The companion tiering-with-deployable run adds the production N=5 operating points (text 4-of-5, image 3-of-5; the 55maps thresholds) so operating-point sensitivity is tiered too. Era-2 487-tile test scope, 384px, gemini-3-flash proposer. This is the FINDING that realises the registered pv-diag-384-consensus-calibration sweep.
deviations: None for the operating-point selection: analysis-summary.md (H3) preregisters 'threshold sweep curves showing optimal (N, threshold) combinations' and 'voted F1 vs single-pass mean F1' against the test tiles, so the best-operating- point characterisation is the preregistered method (not in-sample/E56 -- that rule governs the verifier prob_t diagnostics, a distinct case; see E56 Update 2026-06-06).
E49/E51 (T=0.7 production carry-forward temperature; HIGH thinking) -- the characterised configurations, carried forward from Phase 2b.
Production operating point reported alongside best: text 4-of-5, image 3-of-5 (the 55maps deployment thresholds); the best-minus-N5 delta is the within-test operating-point sensitivity.
analyses.predicted_outcome: H3: consensus voting over K proposer passes improves localisation F1 over single-pass; the diversity dividend predicts HIGH-thinking (more diverse) pools recover or exceed minimal-thinking under consensus, and that cheap Flash consensus can approach expensive single-pass Pro.
analyses.outcome: Both named claims of the diversity-dividend test are confirmed at the preregistered 20m buffer. Per the preregistered H3 analysis plan (analysis-summary.md: 'compare voted F1 vs single-pass mean F1' + 'threshold sweep curves showing optimal (N, threshold) combinations'), the headline is each configuration's BEST (N, threshold) operating point against the known test-tile ground truth -- the study's purpose is to characterise how well VLM symbol extraction localises mounds, so best-achievable performance is the deliverable, not a confound. Method: round-robin tile-swap permutation (10k perms, seed 42, two-sided; BH-FDR q=0.05) + greedy-clique tiering over a 22-cell board (4 consensus champions + 18 single-pass cells); 197/231 pairs significant -> 7 tiers. (1) DIVERSITY DIVIDEND -- HIGH-thinking consensus significantly exceeds minimal-thinking consensus at matched modality: text +0.153 F1 (BH-p<0.001; MCC +0.239) and image +0.070 F1 (BH-p<0.001; MCC +0.272). The HIGH-thinking pools take the larger consensus gain -- more varied proposals let a high vote threshold prune their false positives. (2) CONSENSUS vs SINGLE-PASS -- every consensus champion significantly beats its matched within-pool single-pass baseline (+0.13 to +0.43 F1, all BH-p<0.001), and the lift persists at the production N=5 operating point (text 4-of-5, image 3-of-5; +0.09 to +0.33 F1). (3) CROSS-ARCHITECTURE HEADLINE -- Tier 1 (the tie_set) is a THREE-member statistical tie: the best Flash HIGH-text consensus (F1 0.814) and the two genuine-Gemini-3-Pro single-pass text leaders (pro-text-high-t-0-0 0.804, pro-text-medium-t-0-0 0.792); the permutation cannot separate Flash-consensus from the Pro leader (p=0.616, BH-p=0.66). Cheap Flash consensus reaches the expensive Pro single-pass tier on localisation F1. OPERATING-POINT SENSITIVITY (characterised, co-headlined): the Tier-1 parity is at the best (N, threshold) point (26-of-30); at the production N=5 carry-forward point (text 4-of-5) the same pool reaches TIER 2 (0.720), tying genuine Pro text at T=0.7 -- a best-minus-N5 delta of ~0.094 F1 (the within-test cousin of the carry-forward-vs-best delta the 55-map generalisation reports). F1-parity is NOT MCC-parity: the Pro text leaders are more tile-precise (MCC 0.790, 11 tile FPs) than the Flash consensus champion (MCC 0.620, 41 tile FPs) -- the metric-dependent-winner pattern of the n1 board persists. Deployment generalisation to unseen maps is the separate question answered by the 55-map runs. Era-2 487-tile test scope, 384px, gemini-3-flash. Artefacts: results/diversity-dividend-384/{tiering-champions,tiering-with-deployable}/tiering_20m.{json,md}; script scripts/consensus_vs_baseline_tiering.py; cell spec planning/diversity-dividend-cells-2026-06-06.json.

N in {5,10,30} are first-N sub-pools (preregistration Section 3.8); the N=5/N=10 consensus GeoJSONs were regenerated via merge_passes (build_phase3_subpool_consensus.py) since only N=30 was materialised on disk. 14-buffer + MCC re-score, Era-1 340-tile, curator GT, gemini-3-flash. The re-scored best-F1@20m operating points reproduce the existing F1-only optima (results/retest/phase3a-consensus/) to ~4 d.p.
analyses.predicted_outcome: H3: consensus voting over K proposer passes improves localisation F1 over single-pass; vote threshold trades precision (high k) for recall (low k); the best-F1 threshold is config-dependent and rises with N.
analyses.outcome: Consensus vote-threshold x N calibration over 18 configs (2 tracks x 3 temperatures x N in {5,10,30}), re-scored at the 14-buffer + MCC standard (Era-1 340-tile, 512px, MINIMAL thinking). Each config's headline operating point is its best-F1@20m vote threshold. Best per track: image T0.7 N30 18-of-30 F1=0.6909 (MCC 0.4416); text T0.3 N30 23-of-30 F1=0.6921 (MCC 0.1807). Best-F1@20m rises with N (full N=30 pools win every cell) and ranges 0.639-0.692 across configs. A pronounced F1-vs-MCC divergence: text consensus localises comparably to image on F1 (~0.69) but has much lower tile-discrimination MCC (text 0.15-0.33 vs image 0.44-0.47) at the F1-optimal (recall-leaning) threshold. This registers the consensus calibration material; the preregistered statistical comparison against single-pass lives in results/retest/phase3a-consensus/. Note the MINIMAL-thinking caveat above — the diversity-dividend (HIGH-thinking) result is retest-phase3a-high / -replication.

analyses._note: Consensus vote-threshold x N calibration sweep for retest-phase3a-high (H3; HIGH thinking; Session 106). Text track only — the image track never ran (only a study_manifest.json). 3 temperatures x N in {5,10,30}; 9 conditions at best-F1@20m. N=5/N=10 sub-pools regenerated via merge_passes. 14-buffer + MCC, Era-1 340-tile, curator GT, gemini-3-flash. This is the HIGH-thinking sibling of retest-phase3a (MINIMAL) and the source of the diversity-dividend contrast.
analyses.predicted_outcome: H3 + diversity dividend: HIGH-thinking proposer pools are more diverse, so a high vote threshold prunes their false positives and consensus recovers or exceeds minimal-thinking consensus.
analyses.outcome: Consensus calibration over 9 HIGH-thinking text configs (3 temperatures x N in {5,10,30}), 14-buffer + MCC, Era-1 340-tile. Best operating points cluster tightly near F1 0.77 at N=30: T1.0 23-of-30 F1=0.7747 (MCC 0.6425, the MCC leader), T0.3 23-of-30 F1=0.7744 (MCC 0.5759), T0.7 22-of-30 F1=0.7729 (MCC 0.5722). This is ~+0.08 F1 above the matched MINIMAL-thinking phase3a text consensus (~0.69) and substantially higher MCC (0.57-0.64 vs 0.15-0.33) — the diversity dividend: HIGH-thinking pools yield more varied proposals that a high vote threshold converts into both better localisation and far better tile discrimination. Best-F1@20m rises with N. Registers the calibration material; the formal HIGH-vs-MINIMAL test is retest-phase3a-replication and the 384px diversity-dividend-384 sibling.

analyses._note: Clean HIGH-vs-MINIMAL thinking replication at T=0.7 text (retest-phase3a-replication, H3; Session 106), built because the original phase3a HIGH/minimal arms both accidentally ran minimal. 2 cells (high, minimal) x N in {5,10,30}; 6 conditions at best-F1@20m. N=5/N=10 sub-pools regenerated via merge_passes. 14-buffer + MCC, Era-1 340-tile, curator GT, gemini-3-flash. The re-scored best operating points reproduce results/retest/phase3a-consensus/replication/ to ~4 d.p.
analyses.predicted_outcome: Diversity dividend: at matched temperature (T=0.7) and modality (text), HIGH-thinking consensus exceeds MINIMAL-thinking consensus because higher-thinking pools are more diverse.
analyses.outcome: Direct HIGH-vs-MINIMAL thinking contrast at T=0.7 text under consensus, 14-buffer + MCC, Era-1 340-tile. At the full N=30 pool HIGH (21-of-30, F1=0.7705, MCC 0.5466) beats MINIMAL (25-of-30, F1=0.7033, MCC 0.3130) by +0.067 F1 and +0.234 MCC; the HIGH advantage holds at N=10 (0.7466 vs 0.7009) and N=5 (0.7129 vs 0.6905). This is the clean confirmation of the diversity dividend that the original phase3a could not provide (both its arms ran minimal): more proposal diversity from higher thinking, pruned by a high vote threshold, lifts both localisation and tile discrimination. Registers the calibration material; the formal paired-permutation test is in results/retest/phase3a-consensus/replication/.

analyses._note: H9 cross-pass diversity study (retest-phase3c; Session 106) — does combining DIVERSE passes (instruction-variant B, image/hard-negative C [track1 only], temperature D, combined E) beat identical passes (baseline A) under consensus? HIGH thinking. One citable condition per (track x H9 condition) cross-variant diversity pool at best-F1@20m (9 conditions; image A-E, text A/B/D/E with C omitted as degenerate). Diversity pools built per the preregistered grouping rule (replication k = run_k of each of the 5 pass-variants) via materialise_phase3c_consensus.py; scored as replicate-mean over 5 replications. 14-buffer + MCC, Era-1 340-tile, curator GT, gemini-3-flash. H9 was REJECTED (see results/phase3c-diversity/).
analyses.predicted_outcome: H9: introducing diversity across the K consensus passes (instruction, image, temperature, or combined) improves accuracy over K identical passes.
analyses.outcome: H9 diversity calibration over 9 cross-variant diversity pools (replicate-mean over 5 replications), 14-buffer + MCC, Era-1 340-tile, HIGH thinking. H9 is REJECTED: at the best-F1@20m operating point each diverse condition is statistically indistinguishable from the identical-pass baseline A. Image (vote 3-of-5): baseline A F1=0.6640 (MCC 0.6603) vs diverse B 0.6682 / C 0.6713 / D 0.6688 / E 0.6705 (MCC 0.648-0.664) — all within ~0.007 F1 of baseline (original paired-permutation p>0.37 for every comparison). Text (vote 4-of-5): baseline A F1=0.7171 (MCC 0.4420) vs B 0.6862 / D 0.7301 / E 0.6943 (MCC 0.44-0.48); only temperature-diversity D edges baseline (+0.013) and even that was not significant (p~0.06). No diversity mechanism delivers a significant gain. Note image diversity pools carry notably high tile-discrimination MCC (~0.66), well above text (~0.45). Registers the calibration material; the preregistered permutation tests are in results/phase3c-diversity/.

analyses.outcome: Era-1 (Gold-Standard 4-map, 512px, 340-tile, curator GT) single-pass baseline board, tiered by round-robin tile-swap micro-F1 permutation (10k perms, seed 42, two-sided; BH-FDR q=0.05; 227/630 pairs significant -> 4 tiers) at the 20m headline buffer. analyses.predicted_outcome: Definitive Era-1 board (H1-H9 cross-cut). H3: consensus voting over K proposer passes beats single-pass on localisation F1; the diversity dividend predicts HIGH-thinking (more diverse) pools recover or exceed minimal-thinking under consensus. analyses.outcome: The DEFINITIVE Era-1 (Gold-Standard 4-map, 512px, 340-tile, curator GT) leaderboard: all 36 single-pass + all 42 consensus cells in one tiered board (dodgy PV-512 excluded, D1), round-robin tile-swap micro-F1 permutation (10k perms, seed 42, two-sided; BH-FDR q=0.05; 2103/3003 pairs significant -> 9 tiers) at 20m. Per the preregistered H3 plan the best (N, threshold) operating point vs the GS test tiles IS the characterisation deliverable (not in-sample). FINDINGS, all matching priors: (1) BEST CONFIG -- Tier 1 (tie_set) is a 6-member statistical tie of HIGH-thinking text consensus at N>=10 (F1 0.759-0.775), led by text-high-t1.0-n30-23of30 (F1 0.775, MCC 0.642); the clean HIGH-vs-MINIMAL replication champion text-high-t0.7-n30-21of30 (0.770) sits in Tier 1 too. (2) CONSENSUS DOMINATES SINGLE-PASS -- every one of the 42 consensus cells (Tiers 1-5, F1 0.639-0.775) outranks every single-pass cell; the best single pass, canonical-last (0.631), is rank 43. (3) DIVERSITY DIVIDEND, TIERED -- HIGH-thinking text consensus (~0.77, Tiers 1-2) >> minimal text consensus (~0.69-0.70, Tiers 3-4) >> text single-pass (~0.60, Tier 6). (4) F1-vs-MCC DIVERGENCE -- image consensus pools localise lower on F1 but discriminate far better at tile level: the image-h9 diversity pools sit at F1 ~0.664-0.671 / MCC ~0.65-0.66, well above text consensus at matched F1 (text-t0.3-n30 0.692 F1 / 0.181 MCC); text-HIGH wins BOTH (F1 0.77, MCC 0.55-0.64). (5) H9 DIVERSITY does not separate from the identical-pass baseline-A within its tier (consistent with the prior H9 rejection). All 78 cells reproduce their published F1@20m to <=0.0001. gemini-3-flash; MINIMAL thinking except phase3a-high/-replication (HIGH). The clean Era-1 proposer-verifier grid (gated Stage D) will be folded in by re-tiering this board. Artefacts: results/era1-leaderboard/tiering_20m.{json,md}; script scripts/era1_leaderboard_tiering.py.

analyses.outcome: Tile-size characterisation across 256/384/512 px (F1@20m), gemini-3-flash, GS 4-map curator GT. The optimal tile size is ARCHITECTURE-DEPENDENT, consistent with the FP-filtering mechanism (Obs 351, Obs 179, Obs 171). CLEAN ISOLATION (hold architecture x modality x thinking x temperature constant, vary only size): single-pass text climbs monotonically with tile size (256=0.342 < 384=0.520 < 512=0.606) — with no FP filter, larger tiles give cleaner proposals; single-pass image is flat (384~0.600 ~ 512~0.586). Text MINIMAL consensus still prefers 512 (+0.02..+0.05 over 384 across T0.3/0.7/1.0) — a weak filter. Text HIGH consensus FLIPS to 384 (T0.7 0.814 > 512 0.773; T0.3 0.789 > 0.774; T1.0 ~tie) — the strong diversity+vote filter realises 384's higher recall. BEST-ACHIEVABLE FLASH CEILING per size: single-pass 512 (0.631) > 384 (0.520) > 256 (0.342); consensus 384 (0.814) > 512 (0.775) > 256 (0.460). So 384 owns the consensus ceiling, 512 owns the single-pass ceiling, and 256 trails under both. KEY GAP: 256 consensus+VERIFIER (the one architecture where 384 wins decisively) is untested — pv-diag-256 is consensus-only — so 'does 256 overwhelm even the verifier' is open (Obs 351); a cheap 256 consensus+PV run would close it. Pro single-pass ran only at 384 (pro-text 0.792, pro-image MCC 0.868) — shown for context, not a tile-size comparison.
